tools.name: start_episode
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a podcast, interview, stream or other video turned into short clips. An audio-only episode (MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG or FLAC) works too: its clips come out as captioned vertical videos drawn with an audio template. With a video or audio file attached in the chat, pass it as fi

tools.name: get_episode
tools.description: Use this when the user asks how an episode is going, whether it is ready, or what clips were found. Returns one status for the whole pipeline (waiting_for_upload, uploading, transcribing, finding_clips, ready or failed) and, once ready, the found clips with number, ref, title, opening line, length a

tools.name: make_clips
tools.description: Use this when the user picks found clips to make. Cuts each one from the episode and renders it with captions burned in, in one step. Pass the numbers or refs get_episode listed (refs in brackets are fine), or any stretch of the episode as {"start_seconds", "end_seconds", "title"}. Optional style, c

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to know whether a clip is cut or rendered, or wants the finished file. Pass the job_id from make_clips or restyle_clip, or a clip_id for that clip's latest render. Returns the status, progress, a still from the clip and, when finished, a short download link. Pass wait: t

tools.name: restyle_clip
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a made clip changed and rendered again: a different caption style, bigger or smaller captions, captions moved up or down, the hook title turned on, off or reworded, or the whole video shown instead of cropped (fit, background). The change is saved on the clip and a new r

tools.name: list_styles
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to know which caption looks they can choose from. Returns each style's id, name, a one-line description and a link to a preview picture. Pass styles to look up particular ones. Do not use to change a clip (use restyle_clip or make_clips).

tools.name: find_clips_about
tools.description: Use this when the user wants clips from an episode on a particular topic or for a particular audience, e.g. "clips about creativity for artists" or "moments for young entrepreneurs". Searches the episode again for moments that fit the focus, skipping clips already found, and adds what it finds to th

tools.name: get_visual_style
tools.description: Use this when someone gives a Slice style ref (like "sref-V4RYN2"), names a style from tryslicemedia.com/styles, or pastes a prompt that says to call get_visual_style. Returns the style's look and feel: palette, materials, motion and type rules, what it suits, how to use it in a clip, and the STORY

tools.name: suggest_visual_styles
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to see Slice's style library, and only then. When someone wants visuals or animation and has no style, design your own looks for the clip first (owner, 1 November 2026: the library is being reworked); never list library styles in the chat unasked. With a library request

tools.name: get_clip_edit
tools.description: Use this when you are about to fix a made clip, first: returns every word with its index, text and times on the clip (seconds), whether it is a filler ("um"), whether a long pause follows it, and whether it is already cut; plus the hook title, the caption look, the trim, the frame (shape, layout, cr

tools.name: cut_words
tools.description: Use this when the person wants to remove words, every filler, or long pauses from a made clip, the way the Slice editor's clean-up does: the sound and the captions both, with breathing room kept so it never sounds choppy. Pass words as a list of indexes from get_clip_edit, or {"fillers": true}, or {

tools.name: set_hook_title
tools.description: Use this when the person wants to reword, turn on or off, or restyle the title card at the top of a made clip. style is a box such as "white box", "black box" or "lime word" (or a title template id). Saves the clip only, no render.

tools.name: edit_captions
tools.description: Use this when the person wants to change captions on a made clip, applied in order. Word indexes and seconds come from get_clip_edit. set_text {word, text} fixes a word; split {word} starts a new caption at it; join {word} joins its caption to the one before; line_break {word} breaks the line before

tools.name: set_trim
tools.description: Use this when the person wants to change where a made clip starts or ends, or to cut out any stretch in the middle, in seconds on the clip (get_clip_edit gives the word times). remove [{start_seconds, end_seconds}] cuts stretches (sound, picture and their captions); restore [...] puts cut stretches

tools.name: set_caption_style
tools.description: Use this when the person wants to change a made clip's captions, anything a person can change by hand, without a render: style (list_styles names), size (smaller, bigger, small, medium, large, extra_large), position (up, down, top, middle, lower, bottom) or an exact height (caption_y, e.g. to keep t

tools.name: set_frame
tools.description: Use this when the person wants to change how a made clip's picture is framed, anything the Slice editor's Frame tab and Layouts do, with no render. aspect: 9:16, 4:5, 1:1, 16:9, 3:4, source (ask the person which shape first). layout: follow-speaker, follow-both, two-people, face-on-top, face-corner,

tools.name: undo_edit
tools.description: Use this when the person wants to take back changes you (the person's AI) made to a clip with the edit tools, newest first, the same as Undo in the Slice editor. A storyboard moment taken off the clip (in the editor or by you) is undone here too: it comes back as it was (edit_id "moment:<id>" from l

tools.name: templates
tools.description: Use this when the person likes a look and wants to keep it, or wants their saved look on clips. The same saved templates as the Slice editor's Saved styles. kind: style (the caption look with logo, framing, stacking and caption rules; "setup" also keeps the clip's shape, layout, hook title look and

tools.name: read_captions
tools.description: Use this when the user asks what a clip says, what is on screen at a particular moment, which caption contains a word or a typo, or who said something. It is also the only way to get a caption's id, so read it first whenever a later step needs to name one caption. Narrow with at_seconds, a from/to r

tools.name: transcribe_audio
tools.description: Use this when the user wants the words: speech in an audio or video file turned into text, from a podcast, interview, lecture, meeting or voice note. Accepts a file the user attached (file) or a direct https link to a media file such as .mp3, .m4a, .wav or .mp4 (url). Returns the transcript with spe

tools.name: transcription_status
tools.description: Use this when transcribe_audio returned status "processing", to check whether the transcript is finished and get its text. Pass the transcription_id it returned. Call it again after a short wait while the status is still "processing". Only answers in the conversation (or Slice account) that started

tools.name: email_transcript
tools.description: Use this only when the user explicitly asks for a finished transcript to be emailed to them. Needs a Slice sign-in, asked for on first use, and sends the .txt, .srt and .vtt files only to the confirmed email address on that Slice account, never to another address. Each transcript can be emailed one

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "make_clips" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use this when the user picks found clips to make. Cuts each one from the episode and renders it with captions burned in, in one step. Pass the numbers or refs g…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start_episode, get_episode, suggest_visual_styles, read_captions, transcription_status · Private data: start_episode, make_clips, get_job, templates, transcribe_audio, email_transcript · Public sink: start_episode, set_frame, email_transcript · Destructive: start_episode, cut_words, edit_captions, set_trim, set_caption_style, templates.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start_episode, get_episode, suggest_visual_styles, read_captions, transcription_status · Private data: start_episode, make_clips, get_job, templates, transcribe_audio, email_transcript · Public sink: start_episode, set_frame, email_transcript · Destructive: start_episode, cut_words, edit_captions, set_trim, set_caption_style, templates

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "start_episode" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
